outcome: timing of very early microbial colonization
cohort: 18 healthy mother-infant dyads were included in the study.
finding: The study confirmed the existence of a meconium microbiome and the absence of a placental microbiome, found significant sharing of oral microbiota (Streptococcus and Veillonella) between mothers and infants, and associated vaginal delivery and exclusive breastfeeding with enhanced infant microbial richness and diversity.
mod_finding: Vaginal delivery was strongly associated with enhanced microbial richness and diversity in infants.
